Perform Vertex Set Enrichment Analysis

run_vsea.Rd

Runs a ranked-list enrichment analysis (Vertex Set Enrichment Analysis), calculating a Normalized Enrichment Score (NES) and a False Discovery Rate (FDR) q-value for each term using a permutation-based null distribution.

Usage

run_vsea(
  object,
  element_ranks,
  scoring_statistic = "log2_Anscombe_ratio",
  n_permutations = 1000,
  n_cores = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

# S4 method for class 'ECTermScoring'
run_vsea(
  object,
  element_ranks,
  scoring_statistic = "log2_Anscombe_ratio",
  n_permutations = 1000,
  n_cores = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

object

An ECTermScoring object.

element_ranks

A named list or vector of element ranks.

scoring_statistic

The score to use for enrichment (e.g., "log2_Anscombe_ratio").

n_permutations

The number of permutations to generate the null distribution, 1000 by default.

n_cores

Number of cores to use for parallel processing. Defaults to detectCores() - 1. Set to 1 for serial execution (or on Windows).

seed

An optional random seed for reproducibility.

Value

A list containing a single data frame: max_score_summary. The data frame is sorted by fdr_q_value and contains:

  • term_id: The term identifier.

  • max_score: The maximum running enrichment score observed.

  • nes: Normalized Enrichment Score.

  • fdr_q_value: Empirical False Discovery Rate.

  • term_size: Number of elements in the term.

  • rank_at_max: The element rank at which the score peaked.

  • observed_ec: The number of observed edges at the peak.

Details

This version focuses solely on identifying positive enrichment, i.e., the maximum score for each term

Methods (by class)

  • run_vsea(ECTermScoring): Method for ECTermScoring objects.

Examples

library(EdgeCount)
library(data.table)

# Load data
data(sample_ects)

# Random uniform ranking
element_ranks <- setNames(
  sample(seq_along(sample_ects@elements)),
  sample_ects@elements
)

# VSEA analysis
vsea_results <- run_vsea(
  sample_ects,
  element_ranks,
  n_permutations = 10, # Low for speed
  n_cores = 2,
  seed = 1
)

print(head(vsea_results$max_score_summary))
